summary: Christopher Kelley is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD from Columbia University. He has taught at Columbia University, The New School, and Brooklyn College, and founded the Columbia Society for Comparative Philosophy.

Christopher Key Chapple is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He held posts at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions (attested 1982), Stony Brook University (attested 1983), and Loyola Marymount University (attested 2001–2017).

Christopher Minkowski is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Harvard College, the University of Delhi, and Harvard University. He was a professor at Cornell University (1989–2006) and Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (2005–2023).

Christopher Pinney is a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar. His appointments include the Australian National University (~1990–1992), University College London (~1993), the University of Chicago (~1998), and Northwestern University (~2006–2007), among others.

Christopher S. George is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Columbia University under Royal W. Weiler, founded the American Institute of Buddhist Studies (1972), and was a professor at IASWR (attested 1982).

Christopher S. Queen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. At Harvard University (~1989–2011), he served as Dean of Students for Continuing Education and lectured on the Study of Religion, Buddhism, and World Religions.

Christopher Wallis is an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Rochester, Oxford (under Alexis Sanderson), and UC Berkeley (PhD, under Robert P. Goldman and Alexander von Rospatt). He served as a guest lecturer at Naropa University (attested 2020).

Chu-tsing Li was a Chinese art historian and sinologist who studied at the University of Nanking and the University of Iowa. He taught English at Nanking (1943–1947) and art history at Iowa (~1956–1966) and the University of Kansas (1966).

Chun-i Tang was a philosopher and sinologist educated at National Central University and other institutions under mentors like Shili Xiong. He was a professor at National Central University, New Asia Institute, and the founding chair professor at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Chun-min Yen is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello. He also studied under Todd Brown, Chanyun, and Sheng Yen.

Chuta Ito was an architectural historian and archaeologist who graduated from the University of Tokyo (~1889–1892). He held major academic posts at the University of Tokyo (~1905–1928) and Waseda University (~1928–1937).

Chögyam Trungpa was a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Khenpo Gangshar and at the University of Oxford, served as spiritual advisor at the Young Lamas Home School (1959–1963), and founded Naropa University (1973).
Chöje Akong Tulku Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1967 he founded the Kagyu Samye Ling Monastery and Tibetan Centre, where he later served as abbot (attested 2009).

Chökyi Gyatso studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Khakyab Dorje. He also taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
Chökyi Nyima studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Chökyi Nyinche studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Shechen Gyaltsab. He also taught Dilgo Khyentse.
Chönyi Drolma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Thinley Norbu Rinpoche, Lama Tharchin Rinpoche, and Ngawang Zangpo (all attested 2011).

Chüan-ying Yen is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned a PhD at Harvard University (attested 1986), where she studied with John M. Rosenfield, Chu-tsing Li, and John Hay.

Chün-fang Yü is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned her degree at Columbia University (~1965–1973). She held posts at Rutgers University (~1972–2001) and Columbia University (~2001).

Clara Sue Kidwell was a historian who studied at the University of Oklahoma. She taught at UC Berkeley (~1974–1993), directed Native American studies at the University of Oklahoma (1995), and served as director at UNC Chapel Hill (~2007–2011).
